column2: Meteorites! Tiny but bright. I'm collecting them in a bag as a keepsake.
I wished that everyone stays healthy and that the till always keeps some change.
I wished a meteorite would land on my foot. Gently. And not on mine.
My wish is that we reach the end and lose no one along the way.
The Moon in the Window
Tonight the Moon is closest to Earth! See? It almost touches the shop window.
I wonder what it thinks of our shop.
It'll say: “I don't ask for rent. I'll take cheese.”
I tried to bite off a piece. It's not cheese. It's like a warmed-up white brick.
The Moon slowly blinked in reply, and everyone decided it was an apology.
The Alien Customer
The shop door opened with a soft hiss. A violet creature with three eyes walked in.
That's an alien! Probably from a very distant planet. Say something friendly.
Good day! Would you like to buy something to remember Earth by?
The creature pointed at a bag of candy, exhaled a glowing puff and paid with a shining pebble.
The most valuable currency I've ever seen. Please don't give change by the bucket.
The Countdown
On the highest roof a rocket came to life. Everyone gathered around: residents, guests, even the cat star.
Everything's ready! Only the countdown left: ten, nine, eight...
Orbit, will you fly?
I'm staying here until you come back. Someone has to turn the lights on.
The rocket soared and burst into a million sparks. In fact it was festival fireworks.
The Last Star
At night Capy gazed at the sky for a long time. Among the stars hung one that blinked in time with ticking.
That's me. Or rather, my colleague from the future. Sends his regards.
Aren't you lonely up there?
I'm a Watch. For me loneliness is when nobody asks what time it is.
Orbit gave Capy a tiny star as a keepsake. “It will glow if you need it,” he said.
The City That Never Sleeps
The streets glowed pink and turquoise, and holograms drifted over the roofs announcing great discounts.
I'm Lumi, a firefly on a permanent night shift. I help the neon signs not get tired.
Is it never dark here?
Only when we turn on “cozy mode”. Then everyone just glows more quietly.
A flying car flickered overhead, and the wind smelled of ozone and bubblegum.
Capy's Hologram
Above the shop a giant hologram of Capy flared up with a smile and the words “YOUR LUCKY SELLER”.
That's not me. I don't have whiskers like that.
I touched it up a little. Now you look like a movie star. For free.
I did the math: it raised customer traffic by twenty percent. Why the whiskers in particular is unclear.
Let it hang for now. But next time, no whiskers.
Robot Guards
Two robots with bright lenses were placed at the entrance. They bowed in sync to every visitor.
I taught them to stand without yawning. It's the hardest thing I've ever done.
They see everything in infrared. They have a special weakness for the raccoon.
They suspect me. Even when I'm doing nothing. That's discrimination.
Just don't carry eight bags of coffee from the shop next door.
Flying Taxis
Taxis with translucent domes whooshed down the street. Each glowed its own colour and slammed its doors loudly.
There's a free one! Hop in, Capy: three minutes to the mall.
Three minutes? I can walk it in two.
True, but the taxi has music and serves hot tea.
Capy rode, drank tea and watched the neon rivers below. For the first time in ages, she wasn't in a hurry.
The Night Market
Once a month our night market opens. They sell everything, from fireflies in jars to stardust.
I already found a stall of “genuine fakes”. Honest business: honestly forged.
Everyone, please keep receipts. The market doesn't give any, so we note them by hand.
Look at that lamp! It glows a different colour depending on your mood.
In Capy's hands the lamp turned soft gold. “Calm,” the seller read.
The Masked Hacker
Suddenly every sign in the city showed the same thing: a smiling raccoon face and the word “HELLO”.
We've been hacked! Someone is sending their own jokes to the signs!
It wasn't me. I only gave someone a password. For a small fee.
Shnyr, whose password was it?
Well... mine. I love it. “penny123”. Made it up myself. Just now.
The Blackout
The city went dark in an instant. Signs, holograms, flying cars: everything froze, as if someone had switched off the world.
I know what to do! All fireflies, to me! We'll light the street ourselves.
Thousands of tiny lights rose above the roofs. Not as bright as neon, but warm.
Look. The city glows by itself.
I never told anyone, but I like the street like this. It makes me want to stay.
Shnyr Joins the Team
Light returned at dawn. Shnyr stood before Capy, shifting from paw to paw, holding all his “trophy” treasure.
Here. Everything I ever “borrowed”. Take it. And take me onto the team. Honestly.
You won't play around with the till, will you?
I stopped. I like it better when we count coins together.
Welcome to the team, Shnyr. Now golden customers can't get away from you.
That was the last era of the circle. But time travel is a spiral. A new circle begins.
The Teapot That Ran Away
Steam rose above the tea house like a tiny cloud. A fox hovered by the door, staring at an empty shelf.
Hi, I'm Sora. My best teapot went for a walk by itself. I looked everywhere, and it's probably looking for me.
A teapot left without an exit receipt. That's a violation. Calculating damages.
Easy. Who saw where it rolled?
I saw. It rolled after a lantern toward the bridge. I was only walking the same way. By chance. With a sack.
The Dragon Wants Tea
A long green dragon hung above the roofs and peered curiously into the tea house window.
He comes every morning. I pour his tea into a saucer. He drinks, then gives the whole street a breeze.
A dragon drinking from a saucer? The most elegant guest I've ever seen.
And how does he say thanks?
The dragon made a slow loop above the street and tiny sparkles fell from his whiskers. Everyone froze in delight.
The Lantern Festival
The town was preparing for a festival. Paper lanterns swayed on every roof, and the animals were thinking up wishes.
Twenty lanterns slipped off the rope. I swept them all up, but they floated away again by themselves.
That's normal: lanterns love height. Just don't release them without a wish inside.
Then let everyone make a wish, and we'll release them together above the street.
I made one wish. I won't tell anyone. It's about lanterns. And a sack.
The Waving Cat
A white lucky cat stood by the till with a raised paw. The paw had been waving for three days and showed no sign of stopping.
Every wave is a coin that never reached the till. I measured. Now I have the numbers.
He waves because he's waiting for someone. A lucky cat waves until somebody really notices him.
Then smile at him and let him stop.
Everyone smiled at the cat. The paw slowed, lowered, and the cat contentedly closed his eyes. The coins in the till jingled on their own.
The Vending Machine of Surprises
On the corner stood a vending machine that gave a different drink each time: matcha, lemonade, sakura latte, bubble soda.
I put in one coin and it gave four cans and thanked me. It wasn't me. It did it itself.
The machine runs at a loss. Who maintains it?
Nobody. He just likes it when someone smiles over every drink.
Then he's our best employee. Let's not pay him, just smile.
The Sakura That Wouldn't Bloom
By the bridge stood an old sakura with bare branches. All the other trees had bloomed long ago, but she stayed silent.
She's sad. People used to sit with her every day, and now everyone hurries past.
Then I'll bring a bench and tea, and we'll sit.
Let's all sit together. Even five minutes. No till.
They sat. Then a first pink bud appeared on a branch, and a second, and a tenth. By evening the tree stood in a pink cloud.
The Night Market
The night market came out: food stalls, lanterns, the clatter of wooden sandals. It smelled of fried dumplings and caramel.
